title: auth: normalize auth header semantics (project/org keys), scoped tokens, CORS and request signing (nonce) + OpenAI compatibility updates
author: Ethan Cole
description: Unifies header semantics for auth across Redwood API and the OpenAI compatibility layer. Motivation: inconsistent handling of project vs org keys and scoped tokens caused surprising behavior at gateways and CORS boundaries, and streaming sessions could be dropped when fallback auth paths were exercised. This PR: 1) introduces explicit header normalization rules so Authorization: Bearer <token> maps to internal X-Redwood-Auth-Type/X-Redwood-Project/X-Redwood-Org headers when appropriate; 2) adds support for scoped tokens (scope metadata preserved and enforced in middleware) including a new format and check hooks; 3) implements a short-lived nonce header (X-Redwood-Nonce) and server-side nonce replay protection used by request signing flows; 4) tightens CORS handling for token-bearing requests and ensures preflight behavior is explicit for project/org key endpoints; 5) updates the OpenAI compatibility layer so OpenAI-style requests using project-scoped or org-scoped tokens are accepted when scopes match, with graceful failures and clear error messages when scopes are insufficient; 6) retains streaming stability by plumbing auth context into the streaming runtime so fallback/redirects do not orphan active streams; 7) updates SDKs (Python/TS) to expose scoped token creation helpers and automated nonce signing for signed requests; 8) adds integration and unit tests covering replay protection, CORS preflight cases, and streaming auth transitions. Implementation notes: changes are behind a feature flag (auth.header_normalization) enabled for rollout cohorts. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is preserved for most users but stricter CORS semantics and nonce enforcement are opt-in during rollout. See linked Linear items for rollout and monitoring plan.

review_comments: Priya Nair: Left a couple of suggestions on the nonce TTL and eviction strategy — replay cache size could grow under heavy traffic, please add an eviction policy and metrics.
Ethan Cole: Added an LRU-backed eviction with configurable max_entries and emitted metrics (auth.nonce_cache.size, auth.nonce.replays) in the next commit.
Liam O'Connor: Can we make the header normalization opt-in behind a feature flag so we can rollout safely? Also want unit tests for the middleware behavior.
Ethan Cole: Implemented feature flag auth.header_normalization with default off for GA, added unit tests for normalization and a matrixed integration test for streaming fallback transitions.
Jasmine Wu: SDK changes look good, but please document the scoped token format and the recommended rotation cadence in docs.
Ethan Cole: Added docs section and sample curl/bcrypt examples for token creation and rotation.
release_notes: Introduce header normalization for auth, scoped token support, nonce-based request signing, and tighter CORS semantics. Feature gated behind auth.header_normalization for staged rollout. SDK helpers added for scoped token creation and nonce signing.
